answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs. Whether an agent sells cedar furniture, velvet fabric, or comet tracking data, the same bond applies. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore requires 1,000 bonds: splitting one wallet does not multiply access. The attacker must tie up real capital for a month per batch, making mass identities costly even if none wins a job.
